prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1493; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported in Conroe, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just give you the details of what happened, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine, but I do need your name on the recording for our file.

A: Understood. It's the policyholder's driver, the person in the vehicle at the time.

Q: Thank you. Can you describe where you were when the collision occurred?

A: I was driving on a two-lane road heading toward a shopping area. It was a clear afternoon and traffic was moderate.

Q: What happened just before the impact?

A: The other car drifted into my lane around a curve. I braked and steered to the right, but we still made contact nearly head on. It wasn't a hard hit, more of a jolt.

Q: What was your speed at the time?

A: Probably around 20 or 25 miles per hour. I wasn't going fast.

Q: Did either airbag deploy?

A: No, they did not.

Q: Did you go to a medical facility after the collision?

A: Yes, I was checked out the same day. My neck felt stiff and sore, and the doctor diagnosed a neck strain. I've been doing physical therapy since then.

Q: Have you had any prior neck or back complaints?

A: No, nothing serious. I had some stiffness years ago after lifting something, but it resolved on its own.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm still having headaches and some trouble turning my head to the left. I'd like to keep my records updated for you.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
